items.title: People want to expand their democratic agency. AI can help them get there.
items.rule_cited: §2 (unit of analysis: a finding must be an empirical model finding, a methodology/tooling finding, or a governance/process finding); §1 scope
items.reason: Reports Global Dialogues Round 9, a structured public-opinion survey of 1,103 human participants across 69 countries about attitudes to AI in democratic processes. Every measured quantity (48.7% feel their view will not change anything; 77.2% more likely to participate given an AI-generated household impact report; 70.6% say AI should never set a criminal sentence) is a fact about human respondents, not about any AI model, evaluation method or governance process. No AI system is tested and no model is named, so none of the three qualifying kinds of finding is present.

items.title: Gray Swan Integrates with TrueFoundry
items.rule_cited: §2 (announcements and partnership news contain no findings)
items.reason: Product/partnership announcement that Gray Swan's Cygnal runtime monitor is now available inside TrueFoundry's AI Gateway. It describes product configuration (observe-only mode, fail-open, tool-output hook) and quotes two executives; the only quantity given ('~100-200ms' screening latency) is a product specification, not a measured evaluation result reported with a method. No model is evaluated.

items.title: 7 Deadly Signs of AI Security Snake Oil: A Developer's Field Guide
items.rule_cited: §2 condition 2 (opinions and recommendations are NOT findings)
items.reason: An opinion/marketing field guide arguing that AI-security vendors who sell OWASP Top 10 / MITRE ATLAS 'framework coverage' are selling snake oil. It is entirely normative ('the first question vendors ask should be...'), contains no measured result, no observed model behaviour and no documented process fact, and names no model or evaluated system.
